delivered.statement: Blinkit achieved EBITDA breakeven this quarter
Contribution margin expanded 90 basis points despite 6% store throughput decline
EBITDA margin expanded 130 basis points quarter-on-quarter
Achieved 130% YoY like-for-like growth in quick commerce
211 net store additions in Q3 FY26
90% of Blinkit business shifted to inventory model from marketplace

themes: Quick commerce breakeven achieved; margins improving via operating leverage and scale
Competitive intensity high with irrational pricing; management taking tactical delivery fee cuts
Assortment expansion strategy driving customer engagement but diluting per-store throughput metrics
District Pass membership program launched to drive multi-category usage and cross-selling
Capex per store increasing for automation and warehousing infrastructure investments
Tier 2/3 city expansion with similar unit economics to Tier 1 markets
risks: Competitive intensity unpredictable; irrational competitors using zero-fee and heavy discounting affecting margins
Quarterly margin trajectory highly volatile; management unable to forecast near-term expansion pace
New labor code impacts unclear: social security contributions and gratuity rules not yet operationalized
GST demand benefit not fully realized; supply chain transition challenges in Q3
analyst_pushback: Store throughput down 6% QoQ despite margin gains unexplained - management blamed assortment expansion lowering per-SKU velocity
100% growth guidance now needs 3,500-4,000 stores vs 3,000 stated earlier - Akshant denied ever committing to 3,000-store level
Why assume margin expansion continues at same 90-130 bps pace? - Management said margins multi-variable, competition not linear factor
Competition shown irrational yet barely impacting market share visibly - Akshant countered: competition does impact margins, growth, decisions differently
tone_evidence: Confident on long-term business model and margin targets but defensive on near-term predictability. Repeatedly declined quarterly margin forecasts citing volatility.
